questions.q: A multicore processor in which each core executes its own instruction stream on its own data is classified in Flynn's taxonomy as
questions.exp: Multiple independent instruction streams operating on multiple data streams is MIMD.

questions.q: The auto-increment addressing mode is especially useful for
questions.exp: The register used as pointer is incremented automatically after each access, stepping through consecutive elements.

questions.q: A disk has 4 platters (both surfaces used), 1000 tracks per surface, 100 sectors per track and 512 bytes per sector. Taking 1 MB = 10⁶ bytes, its capacity is approximately
Which cache mapping technique needs no replacement algorithm because each memory block maps to exactly one line?
questions.exp: In direct mapping a block has a single possible line, so there is no choice of victim.

questions.q:
Match the I/O technique with its description:
1. Programmed I/O   2. Interrupt-driven I/O   3. DMA
P. CPU continuously tests device status
Q. Device signals the CPU when it is ready
R. Controller moves a block directly between device and memory
questions.exp: Programmed I/O polls, interrupt-driven I/O waits for a device signal, DMA transfers blocks without CPU intervention.

questions.q: A system bus is 32 bits wide, runs at 100 MHz and transfers one word per clock cycle. Its maximum data transfer rate is
questions.exp: 4 bytes × 100 × 10⁶ transfers per second = 400 MB/s.

questions.q: A stack machine executes: PUSH 4, PUSH 6, PUSH 2, SUB, MUL, PUSH 5, ADD. SUB computes (second from top) - (top) and MUL, ADD act on the top two items. The final value on the stack is
questions.exp: Stack: 4,6,2 → SUB gives 6-2=4 → 4,4 → MUL gives 16 → PUSH 5 → ADD gives 21.

questions.q: A processor has a byte-addressable memory and fixed 32-bit instructions. If the PC is 0x1000, what is its value after three sequential instructions have been fetched?
questions.exp: Each instruction is 4 bytes, so PC = 0x1000 + 12 = 0x100C.

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-volatile semiconductor memory used in solid-state drives (SSDs)?
questions.exp: SSDs store data in NAND flash cells, which retain data without power and have no moving parts.

questions.q:
Statement I: RISC processors typically use hardwired control. Statement II: CISC processors commonly use microprogrammed control.
Which is correct?
questions.exp: Simple RISC instruction sets allow fast hardwired control, whereas complex CISC instruction sets are usually implemented with microprograms.

questions.q: A structural hazard in a pipeline arises when
options: Two instructions need the same hardware resource in the same cycle
An instruction depends on the result of a previous one
A branch changes the program counter
questions.exp: Structural hazards are resource conflicts, e.g. a single memory port needed by both instruction fetch and data access.

questions.q: The Zero flag in the processor status register is set when
options: A carry is generated out of the most significant bit
The result of the last ALU operation is zero
The result of the last operation is negative
questions.exp: The Z flag records that the ALU result was all zeros; carry, sign and overflow have their own flags.

questions.q: Register windows, used to speed up procedure calls, are a feature of
questions.exp: RISC designs like SPARC overlap sets of registers to avoid saving and restoring them on calls.

questions.q: A fully associative cache with 3 lines uses LRU replacement and is initially empty. Block references arrive in the order 1, 2, 3, 1, 4, 2. The number of misses is
questions.exp: 1 M, 2 M, 3 M, 1 H, 4 M (evicts 2), 2 M (evicts 3): total 5 misses.

questions.q: A hard disk rotates at 7200 RPM. Its average rotational latency is approximately
questions.exp: One rotation takes 60/7200 = 8.33 ms; average latency is half of that, 4.17 ms.

questions.q: The number of bits that a CPU can process as a single unit in one operation is called its
questions.exp: Word length is the natural unit of data (e.g. 32 or 64 bits) the processor handles at once.

questions.q: In programmed I/O, the CPU repeatedly checking the status register of a device until it is ready is called
questions.exp: Repeatedly testing device status in a loop (busy waiting) is polling.

questions.q: A 16-bit instruction has a 4-bit opcode and three register address fields of equal size. How many registers can each field address?
questions.exp: Remaining bits = 12, so each field has 4 bits and can address 2⁴ = 16 registers.

questions.q: A non-pipelined unit takes 50 ns per instruction. A 5-stage pipeline with 10 ns stages executes 100 instructions. The speedup obtained is approximately
questions.exp: Non-pipelined = 100 × 50 = 5000 ns; pipelined = (5 + 99) × 10 = 1040 ns; speedup = 5000/1040 ≈ 4.81.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a superscalar processor?
options: It can issue more than one instruction per clock cycle using multiple execution units
A single instruction operates on whole vectors of data
It executes exactly one instruction at a time
It shares one execution unit among many threads by time slicing only
questions.exp: Superscalar designs dispatch several instructions per cycle to parallel functional units.

questions.q: Which of the following loses its contents when the power is switched off?
questions.exp: DRAM is volatile and needs power (and refresh) to hold data; ROM, flash and EEPROM are non-volatile.

questions.q: A CPU has a 16-bit address bus. What is the maximum amount of memory it can directly address?
questions.exp: 2¹⁶ = 65536 locations = 64 KB (for byte addressing).

questions.q: In a 4-way low-order interleaved memory, the address 26 is located in which bank?
questions.exp: Bank number = address mod 4 = 26 mod 4 = 2.

questions.q: Which type of interrupt cannot be disabled (masked) by the processor?
questions.exp: A non-maskable interrupt (NMI) is always serviced; used for critical events such as power failure.

questions.q: An instruction ADD R1, @500 uses memory indirect addressing: location 500 holds 800 and location 800 holds the operand. Assuming the instruction occupies one word, how many memory accesses are needed to fetch and complete the operand read?
questions.exp: One access for the instruction, one to read the pointer at 500 and one to read the operand at 800: 3 accesses.

questions.q:
Statement I: A solid-state drive has no mechanical moving parts.
Statement II: The access time of a hard disk includes seek time and rotational latency.
Which is correct?
questions.exp: SSDs are built from flash chips, while a hard disk must move the head to the track and wait for the sector to rotate under it.

questions.q: A processor runs at 2 GHz with an average CPI of 2 and executes 10⁹ instructions. The execution time is
questions.exp: Time = (10⁹ × 2) / (2 × 10⁹) = 1 second.

questions.q: A branch instruction uses PC-relative addressing. The PC (already incremented) holds 1000 and the offset field is +24. The effective address is
questions.exp: Effective address = PC + offset = 1000 + 24 = 1024.

questions.q: Which statement about horizontal microinstructions is correct?
options: They require extensive decoding of encoded fields
They have shorter control words than vertical microinstructions
They allow many micro-operations in parallel with little decoding
They can specify only one micro-operation at a time
questions.exp: Horizontal microcode has long words with one bit per control signal, giving high parallelism and minimal decoding.

questions.q: A branch instruction located at address 2000 uses PC-relative addressing. The PC has already been incremented by 4 and the offset is -12. The branch target address is
questions.exp: Target = PC + offset = 2004 - 12 = 1992.

questions.q:
Match each generation with its key technology:
1. First   2. Second   3. Third   4. Fourth
P. Transistors   Q. VLSI microprocessors   R. Vacuum tubes   S. Integrated circuits
questions.exp: Vacuum tubes (1st), transistors (2nd), ICs (3rd), VLSI microprocessors (4th).

questions.q: Temporal locality of reference means that
options: A recently accessed item is likely to be accessed again soon
Items near a recently accessed item are likely to be accessed soon
Programs access memory only in sequential order
Data is always stored in sorted order
questions.exp: Temporal locality is re-use of the same item in a short time; the nearby-item case is spatial locality.

questions.q: In memory-mapped I/O,
options: Special IN and OUT instructions are mandatory
I/O devices have a completely separate address space
I/O devices can only be used through DMA
Device registers share the memory address space and are accessed using ordinary load/store instructions
questions.exp: Memory-mapped I/O assigns addresses from the memory space to device registers, so normal memory instructions work.

questions.q: Memory access time is 100 ns and the page-fault service time is 8 ms. If the page-fault rate is 1 in 10⁵ accesses, the effective access time is approximately
In DMA, the mode in which the DMA controller takes over the bus for just one memory cycle at a time and then returns it to the CPU is called
questions.exp: In cycle stealing the DMA controller steals single bus cycles from the CPU between its own accesses.

questions.q: A program has 80% of its execution time parallelizable. By Amdahl's law the speedup on 4 processors is
In a half adder, the carry output is given by
questions.exp: Sum = A XOR B and Carry = A AND B.

questions.q: Accessing successive elements of an array inside a loop is most naturally done using which addressing mode?
questions.exp: Indexed addressing adds an index register to a base address; incrementing the index steps through the array.

questions.q: When a maskable interrupt is recognised by a CPU with interrupts enabled, the processor first
options: Stops immediately in the middle of the current instruction
Resets the program counter to zero
questions.exp: Interrupts are checked at instruction boundaries; the current instruction finishes before the PC and state are saved.

questions.q: Daisy chaining in an interrupt system is used for
options: Resolving priority among several interrupting devices
questions.exp: Devices are connected in series; the one nearest the CPU gets the highest priority.

questions.q: A direct-mapped cache of 16 KB uses 64-byte blocks and 32-bit addresses. The total number of tag bits stored in the cache (ignoring valid and dirty bits) is
questions.exp: Lines = 256 (8 index bits), offset = 6 bits, tag = 32 - 8 - 6 = 18 bits; 18 × 256 = 4608 bits.

questions.q: Zero-address instructions are characteristic of which type of machine organization?
questions.exp: Stack machines take operands implicitly from the top of the stack, so arithmetic instructions need no address field.

questions.q: A program has 25% serial code. The maximum speedup possible with an unlimited number of processors, according to Amdahl's law, is
questions.exp: Maximum speedup = 1 / serial fraction = 1 / 0.25 = 4.

questions.q: The stored-program concept, on which modern computers are based, is credited to
questions.exp: The von Neumann architecture keeps both instructions and data in the same memory.

questions.q: How many address lines are needed to address a memory of 16K words?
questions.exp: 16K = 2¹⁴ words, hence 14 address lines.

questions.q: Register R1 holds 2000. Memory[2000] = 3000 and Memory[3000] = 45. After LOAD R2, (R1) using register indirect addressing, R2 contains
questions.exp: In register indirect mode, R1 gives the address 2000; the content of that location, 3000, is loaded into R2.

questions.q: Thrashing in a virtual memory system refers to
options: The cache being overwritten too often
Excessive paging activity so that the system spends more time swapping pages than executing
questions.exp: Thrashing occurs when processes lack enough frames, causing continuous page faults and little useful work.

questions.q: Which technology characterised the third generation of computers?
questions.exp: Third generation computers (1960s) used integrated circuits; transistors were second generation and vacuum tubes first.

questions.q: In a 5-stage pipeline with full forwarding, a load instruction is immediately followed by an instruction that uses the loaded value. How many stall cycles are required?
questions.exp: The loaded data is available only after MEM, so even with forwarding one bubble is needed (load-use hazard).

questions.q: Compared with a 1-bit branch predictor, a 2-bit saturating counter predictor mainly avoids
options: Two mispredictions per execution of a loop (at exit and at re-entry)
questions.exp: A single anomalous outcome (loop exit) does not flip a 2-bit prediction, so a repeated loop is mispredicted only once.

questions.q: Which type of cache miss is completely eliminated by making the cache fully associative (with the same size)?
questions.exp: Conflict misses occur when blocks compete for the same set; a fully associative cache has no such restriction.

questions.q: A Translation Lookaside Buffer (TLB) is
options: A register file for floating-point numbers
A small fast cache holding recently used page-table entries
questions.exp: The TLB caches recent virtual-to-physical translations to avoid a page-table access in memory.

questions.q: The address field of an instruction is 500 and the index register contains 25. Using indexed addressing, the effective address is
questions.exp: Effective address = address field + index register = 500 + 25 = 525.

questions.q: Which of the following is a stated goal/feature of fifth generation computers?
questions.exp: Fifth generation efforts focus on AI, knowledge processing and parallel computing.

questions.q: In a microprogrammed control unit, the microinstructions are stored in
questions.exp: Microprograms reside in a special, usually ROM, control memory.

questions.q: The main advantage of a carry look-ahead adder over a ripple-carry adder is that it
options: Eliminates the need for sum bits
Reduces carry propagation delay by computing carries in parallel
questions.exp: Look-ahead logic generates all carries from generate/propagate signals instead of waiting for each stage.

questions.q: In a write-back cache, the dirty bit of a line indicates that
options: The block was modified after being loaded and must be written to memory before being replaced
The block is locked in the cache
The block has never been accessed
questions.exp: Write-back defers memory updates; the dirty bit marks lines needing a write-back on eviction.

questions.q: In Flynn's classification, a machine with one control unit that broadcasts the same instruction to many processing elements, each working on its own data, is
questions.exp: Single Instruction stream, Multiple Data streams (SIMD), e.g. array and vector processors.

questions.q: A 32-bit instruction format has an 8-bit opcode, two register fields chosen from 32 registers, and the remaining bits as an immediate value. How many bits is the immediate field?
questions.exp: 32 registers need 5 bits each: 32 - 8 - 5 - 5 = 14 bits.

questions.q:
Match each instruction with its category:
1. MOV   2. ADD   3. JMP   4. IN
P. Arithmetic   Q. Data transfer   R. Control transfer   S. Input/output
questions.exp: MOV moves data, ADD is arithmetic, JMP changes control flow and IN reads from an I/O port.

questions.q: On a single-accumulator (one-address) machine, the minimum number of instructions needed to compute X = (A + B) * C is
questions.exp: LOAD A, ADD B, MUL C, STORE X: four instructions.

questions.q: A direct-mapped cache has a total capacity of 4 KB and a block size of 16 bytes. How many cache lines does it have?
questions.exp: Number of lines = 4096 / 16 = 256.

questions.q: A pipeline has a clock period of 2 ns. In the steady state (ignoring start-up), the number of instructions completed per second is
questions.exp: One instruction completes per cycle: 1 / 2 ns = 5 × 10⁸ per second.

questions.q: Which of the following interrupts is normally given the highest priority?
questions.exp: A power-failure interrupt must be handled immediately to save the machine state, so it ranks highest.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): DMA improves system performance for bulk data transfers.
Reason (R): A DMA controller moves data between an I/O device and memory without the CPU executing instructions for each word.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: Because the CPU is not involved word by word, it is free for other work, which is why DMA is efficient for bulk transfers.

questions.q: In the MIPS architecture, an instruction such as add $t0, $t1, $t2 belongs to which instruction format?
questions.exp: Register-register arithmetic instructions use the R-type format.

questions.q: In asynchronous data transfer using handshaking, the two units coordinate using
options: A common clock shared by both
Control signals indicating that data is valid and that data has been accepted
questions.exp: Handshaking uses request/acknowledge (data valid / data accepted) signals instead of a shared clock.

questions.q: A cache is 8 KB, 2-way set associative, with 32-byte blocks. The number of sets is
Which of the following is a CISC architecture?
questions.exp: x86 has variable-length, complex instructions; ARM, MIPS and SPARC are RISC designs.

questions.q: Which type of control unit is generally faster but less flexible to modify?
questions.exp: A hardwired control unit uses fixed logic circuits, so it is faster but harder to change than a microprogrammed one.

questions.q: Which cache write policy updates both the cache and main memory on every write hit?
questions.exp: Write-through writes to the cache and to memory simultaneously, keeping memory always consistent.

questions.q: Which bus carries the signals that indicate whether a memory operation is a read or a write?
questions.exp: Read/write, clock and interrupt signals travel on the control bus.

questions.q: A RISC program executes 1.3 × 10⁹ instructions with CPI 1.2; the equivalent CISC program executes 10⁹ instructions with CPI 3. Both run at the same clock rate. How many times faster is the RISC version?
questions.exp: Cycles: RISC = 1.56 × 10⁹, CISC = 3 × 10⁹; speedup = 3 / 1.56 ≈ 1.92.

questions.q: Main memory is 64 KB and the cache is 1 KB with 16-byte blocks, direct mapped. How many tag bits are in each cache line's tag?
questions.exp: Address = 16 bits; offset = 4 bits; lines = 1024/16 = 64, so index = 6 bits; tag = 16 - 4 - 6 = 6 bits.

questions.q: The Intel 4004, the first commercial microprocessor, is associated with which generation of computers?
questions.exp: Microprocessors built with LSI/VLSI technology mark the fourth generation.

questions.q: Computers using transistors, magnetic core memory and assembly language belong to which generation?
questions.exp: These features define second generation machines (late 1950s to mid 1960s).

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of the von Neumann architecture?
options: Separate memories for instructions and data
Instructions and data share the same memory
questions.exp: Separate instruction and data memories describe the Harvard architecture.

questions.q: A classic 5-stage pipeline (IF, ID, EX, MEM, WB) has no forwarding. The register file is written in the first half and read in the second half of a cycle. An instruction immediately followed by one that uses its result needs how many stall cycles?
questions.exp: The dependent instruction can read the register only in the cycle the producer is in WB, which is 2 cycles later than normal ID.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): RISC processors generally achieve higher pipeline efficiency than CISC processors.
Reason (R): RISC instructions are simple, of fixed length and take a uniform time to execute.
options: Both A and R are false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
questions.exp: Uniform, simple fixed-length instructions make pipeline stages balanced and easy to decode, so the pipeline stalls less.

questions.q: In daisy-chain bus arbitration, the priority of a device is decided by
options: The device number stored in a register
Its position along the chain relative to the arbiter
questions.exp: The grant signal passes through devices in series, so the device nearest the arbiter has the highest priority.

questions.q: How many 1K × 8 RAM chips are required to build a memory of 8K × 16?
questions.exp: 8K/1K = 8 chips along the depth and 16/8 = 2 along the width: 8 × 2 = 16 chips.

questions.q: Which of the following is an optical storage medium?
questions.exp: Blu-ray discs are read with a blue laser; the others are magnetic or flash based.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a technique for reducing the penalty of control (branch) hazards?
questions.exp: Operand forwarding resolves data hazards; the other three deal with branches.

questions.q:
Statement I: Immediate addressing needs no memory reference to obtain the operand (beyond fetching the instruction).
Statement II: Register direct addressing needs one memory reference to obtain the operand.
Which is correct?
questions.exp: In register direct mode the operand is in a register, so no memory reference is needed; Statement II is false.

questions.q: In a pipeline, 20% of instructions are branches and each branch causes 2 stall cycles. Ignoring other stalls, the average CPI is

A 16-bit instruction uses 4-bit address fields and an expanding opcode. There are 14 three-address instructions and 30 two-address instructions. What is the maximum number of one-address instructions possible?
questions.exp: 3-address: 2 of 16 opcodes remain; each gives 16 two-address codes = 32, of which 30 are used, leaving 2; each of those gives 16 one-address codes = 32.

questions.q: In a shared-memory multiprocessor, the cache coherence problem arises because
options: Several private caches may hold different copies of the same memory location
questions.exp: When one processor updates its cached copy, other caches may hold stale values unless a coherence protocol is used.

questions.q:
Match the CPU registers with their roles:
1. PC   2. IR   3. MAR   4. MDR
P. Holds the address of the memory location to be accessed
Q. Holds the data being transferred to/from memory
R. Holds the instruction currently being executed
S. Holds the address of the next instruction
questions.exp: PC holds the next instruction address, IR the current instruction, MAR the memory address and MDR the data word.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Base register addressing helps in program relocation.
Reason (R): Changing the contents of the base register shifts all the effective addresses without modifying the address fields in the instructions.
options: A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.exp: EA = base + displacement, so loading a new base relocates the program without editing instructions.

questions.q: A 4-stage pipeline has stage delays of 20, 30, 25 and 35 ns, and each pipeline register adds 5 ns. The time taken to execute 10 instructions is
questions.exp: Clock = 35 + 5 = 40 ns; cycles = 4 + 9 = 13; time = 13 × 40 = 520 ns.

questions.q: In the instruction ADD R1, #25, the second operand is specified using which addressing mode?
questions.exp: The '#' indicates that the constant 25 is part of the instruction itself, which is immediate addressing.

questions.q: In a content-addressable (associative) memory, a word is located by
questions.exp: CAM compares the search key with all stored words in parallel and returns matching locations.

questions.q: Which CPU register always holds the address of the next instruction to be fetched from memory?
questions.exp: The Program Counter (PC) stores the address of the next instruction and is updated after each fetch.

questions.q: In the IEEE 754 single-precision floating-point format, how many bits are used for the exponent?
questions.exp: Single precision has 1 sign bit, 8 exponent bits and 23 fraction bits.

questions.q: A division by zero during program execution causes an interrupt which is classified as
questions.exp: Interrupts caused by the executing program itself, such as divide-by-zero or overflow, are internal interrupts (traps).

questions.q: A system uses 32-bit virtual addresses and 4 KB pages. The number of pages in the virtual address space is
questions.exp: Page offset = 12 bits, so the page number has 32 - 12 = 20 bits, giving 2²⁰ pages.

questions.q: A program has 40% ALU instructions (CPI 1), 30% load/store instructions (CPI 2) and 30% branches (CPI 3). The average CPI is
A page fault occurs when
options: The CPU tries to write to read-only memory
A required block is not found in the cache
The referenced page is not present in main memory
questions.exp: A page fault is raised when the page needed is not resident in main memory and must be brought in from disk.

questions.q: Which of the following has the smallest access time?
questions.exp: Registers sit inside the CPU and are the fastest level of the memory hierarchy.

questions.q: What is the range of integers that can be represented in 8-bit two's complement form?
questions.exp: n-bit two's complement range is -2^(n-1) to 2^(n-1) - 1, i.e. -128 to +127.

questions.q: Pipelining a processor is mainly an example of which kind of parallelism?
questions.exp: Overlapping the execution of different stages of successive instructions is instruction-level parallelism.

questions.q: Which type of read-only memory can be erased by exposure to ultraviolet light and then reprogrammed?
questions.exp: EPROM has a quartz window for UV erasure; EEPROM is erased electrically.

questions.q: Main memory is 16 MB, the cache is 64 KB, the block size is 32 bytes and the cache is 4-way set associative. The number of tag bits is
questions.exp: Address = 24 bits; offset = 5; lines = 2¹⁶/2⁵ = 2¹¹; sets = 2¹¹/4 = 2⁹; tag = 24 - 5 - 9 = 10 bits.

questions.q: Which of the following interfaces transfers data serially, one bit at a time, over a pair of data lines?
questions.exp: USB is a serial bus, whereas the others listed are parallel interfaces.

questions.q: Why does the CPU save the program counter and status word when an interrupt is accepted?
options: To make the interrupt service routine run faster
To resume the interrupted program correctly after the service routine finishes
questions.exp: The saved context is restored on return from the ISR so the interrupted program continues as if nothing happened.

questions.q: In a vectored interrupt system, the interrupting device supplies
options: The opcode of the next instruction
An address or index that identifies its service routine
questions.exp: The vector lets the CPU jump directly to the correct interrupt service routine without polling devices.

questions.q: The 8-bit two's complement representation of -44 is
A stack grows toward lower addresses and the stack pointer initially holds 5000. After three PUSH operations of 2-byte values, the stack pointer holds
questions.exp: Each push decrements SP by 2: 5000 - 3 × 2 = 4994.

questions.q: In 8-bit two's complement arithmetic, adding +100 and +50 gives
questions.exp: 01100100 + 00110010 = 10010110, which is -106 in two's complement; two positives giving a negative means overflow.

questions.q: A data hazard in which an instruction tries to read a register before a previous instruction has written its result is called
questions.exp: This is Read After Write (RAW), a true data dependence.

questions.q: An ideal 5-stage pipeline (no stalls) executes 100 instructions. How many clock cycles are needed in total?
A device transfers 2000 bytes to memory by DMA in burst mode. The bus is 4 bytes wide and each memory cycle takes 200 ns. For how long is the bus held by the DMA controller?
The cache is accessed first (10 ns) and, on a miss, main memory is then accessed (additional 100 ns). With a hit ratio of 0.9, the average memory access time is
questions.exp: AMAT = hit time + miss rate × miss penalty = 10 + 0.1 × 100 = 20 ns.

questions.q: A direct-mapped cache has 8 lines. Block addresses 2, 10, 2, 3, 2, 3 are referenced in order (cache initially empty). The number of hits is
questions.exp: Blocks 2 and 10 both map to line 2: misses on 2, 10, 2, and a miss on 3; then 2 and 3 hit, giving 2 hits.

questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of a RISC processor?
options: Variable-length instructions with many memory-to-memory operations
A very large number of addressing modes
questions.exp: RISC uses simple fixed-length instructions and only load/store instructions access memory.

questions.q: A 3-frame memory uses FIFO page replacement and starts empty. For the reference string 2, 3, 2, 1, 5, 2, 4, 5, 3, 2, 5, 2 the number of page faults is
questions.exp: Faults occur on 2,3,1,5,2,4,3,5,2 (hits on the repeated 2, 5 and 2 at positions 3, 8 and 10), giving 9 faults.

questions.q: A two-level cache: L1 hit rate 90% with 2 ns access; L2 local hit rate 80% with 10 ns access; main memory 100 ns. The average memory access time is
Which CPU register is used to hold intermediate results of ALU operations in a simple one-address machine?
questions.exp: The accumulator holds one operand and receives the ALU result.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a function of the control unit?
questions.exp: Arithmetic and logic operations are done by the ALU; the control unit only fetches, decodes and sequences operations.

questions.q: The correct sequence of the basic instruction cycle is
questions.exp: An instruction is fetched, then decoded, then executed.
